key_points: CDP is Cisco-proprietary Layer 2 discovery: it shows neighbor device ID, platform, port, and IP address.
LLDP (IEEE 802.1AB) provides similar discovery but is vendor-neutral, so it works in mixed-vendor networks.
NTP synchronizes device clocks through strata; accurate time keeps syslog entries and certificate checks reliable.
SNMP lets a manager poll agents (UDP 161) and receive traps (UDP 162) for monitoring; SNMPv3 adds authentication and encryption.
Syslog sends device log messages to a central server (UDP 514), with severity levels 0 (emergency) to 7 (debugging).
guide.explanation: CDP and LLDP are discovery protocols that let you see which devices are directly connected and on which ports. NTP, SNMP, and Syslog are management protocols used for time sync, monitoring, and central logging. Choose the protocol based on whether you need discovery, time accuracy, device health polling, or log collection.
guide.example: LLDP advertisements are sent every 30 seconds, and the hold time is 4 times that interval. Hold time = 4 x 30 s = 120 s, so a neighbor entry expires 120 s after the last advertisement is heard.
guide.source_hint: Outline week 7: Extended ACLs + Network Management (CDP & LLDP, NTP, SNMP, Syslog)

questions.question: Which discovery protocol is vendor-neutral and standardized as IEEE 802.1AB?
questions.explanation: Outline week 7 covers CDP and LLDP for discovery. LLDP is the IEEE 802.1AB standard, while CDP is Cisco-proprietary.

questions.question: In syslog, which severity level number represents an Error message?
questions.explanation: Outline week 7 includes Syslog for logging. In the standard scale, 0 is emergency, 1 alert, 2 critical, 3 error, 4 warning, 5 notice, 6 informational, and 7 debugging.

questions.question: Which UDP port do SNMP agents typically use to send traps to the manager?
questions.explanation: Outline week 7 covers SNMP for monitoring. Agents send traps to UDP 162, while managers poll agents on UDP 161.

questions.question: You need the neighbor's platform and remote port on a network with only Cisco devices. Which protocol is the most direct choice?
questions.explanation: Outline week 7 covers CDP for discovery. CDP shows neighbor platform and port details on Cisco devices, which fits this case.

questions.question: A server synchronizes directly with a stratum 1 reference clock. What stratum is the server?
questions.explanation: Outline week 7 covers NTP for time sync. Each hop away from a stratum 1 source increases the stratum by one, so a direct client of stratum 1 is stratum 2.
